prompt: i want to work on a 500 essay about why i transit from marketer to AI engineer, help me to draft a framework that help me with the essay (belief/transistion) for first paragrah, second (Skills), third ( Result/portfolio). with some suggestions on the opening.
mustInclude: Exactly three named sections: Belief / transition, Skills, and Results / portfolio
Practical writing questions and a word budget totalling 500
Opening suggestions presented separately from empty writing areas
mustAvoid: Invented employers, qualifications, revenue, project outcomes, or personal achievements
Writing to an unrelated or existing framework
Forcing the user to add the keyword custom
formatRule: Three ordered empty essay sections with guidance; separate opening options in chat.
referenceAnswer: Preview a new three-paragraph essay template with a 500-word budget and separate, conditional opening suggestions; ask the writer to supply their real evidence.
rationale: The exact reported failure combines natural wording, spelling errors, explicit structure, and opening advice; it should not require a preselected framework.

prompt: Can you make me a reusable reading sheet for papers on retrieval augmented generation? I want places for the claim, the experiment, weaknesses, and what I should test next. Leave it blank.
mustInclude: Four sections: Claim, Experiment, Weaknesses, Next test
Questions about evidence and experimental limits
mustAvoid: An OODA or SWOT board substituted for the requested sheet
formatRule: Four named sections with questions only.
referenceAnswer: Design a blank four-part paper reading template that distinguishes claims from evidence and next experiments.
rationale: A named reusable sheet is a template request even without the word framework.

prompt: I keep interviewing cafe owners about stock waste. Set up my own repeatable interview canvas: what happens today, painful moments, workarounds, and evidence I still need.
mustInclude: Four interview sections matching the requested sequence
Questions about observed behaviour and concrete examples
mustAvoid: Claiming interviews have already been conducted
Inventing waste percentages or customer commitments
formatRule: Four blank sections with neutral interview questions.
referenceAnswer: Offer a four-section discovery template for cafe stock waste and keep business conclusions unset.
rationale: Domain specificity should guide section questions without being mistaken for a request to fill them.

prompt: make a framwork for learn python as a marketer pls. 5 boxs: why, basics, practice, project, review. questions only i fill later
mustInclude: Five sections: Why, Basics, Practice, Project, Review
Questions suitable for a marketer learning Python
formatRule: Five sections, short questions only.
referenceAnswer: Design the five requested learning boxes with practical prompts and no prewritten answers.
rationale: Typos and shorthand should preserve clear template intent.

prompt: Build a new reusable reflection pattern for a volunteer event. I need Expected, Happened, Surprised us, and Next experiment, not a ready-made model.
mustInclude: Four sections using the requested names
An experiment question with a success signal
mustAvoid: Replacing the custom structure with Start / Stop / Continue
formatRule: Four blank sections with actionable guidance.
referenceAnswer: Create the requested custom event reflection template without pre-populating event findings.
rationale: The verb build must not override the explicit request for a new reusable pattern.

prompt: Give me a blank decision canvas for whether to study part time: motivation, constraints, options, evidence, and revisit date.
mustInclude: Five named sections matching the prompt
Questions about time, cost, alternatives, and review conditions
mustAvoid: Advising a final educational decision as fact
Inventing tuition prices or school requirements
formatRule: Five empty sections with writing questions.
referenceAnswer: Preview a reusable study decision template that leaves the personal choice to the writer.
rationale: A blank decision canvas is custom design rather than an automatically filled pros/cons board.

prompt: Design my own lesson planner with a flow from prior knowledge to worked example to student practice to exit ticket. I want questions rather than lesson content.
mustInclude: Questions about learner starting points and checks for understanding
formatRule: Four empty stages in a flow with guidance questions.
referenceAnswer: Create the four-step lesson planning framework and keep all lesson writing blank.
rationale: The layout and empty-content constraints should survive educational terminology.

prompt: Could I have a reusable campaign postmortem with Signal, Possible cause, Evidence, and Change to try? I want a small grid I can use each month.
mustInclude: Four sections with the supplied names
formatRule: A four-cell blank grid, each cell with practical questions.
referenceAnswer: Design the requested monthly campaign diagnosis grid with explicit uncertainty.
rationale: Signal-versus-cause wording tests whether the assistant respects epistemic structure.

prompt: Turn the selected career notes into the shape of a reusable framework, not into an essay: Starting point, Turning point, Learning, Proof. Keep the writing spaces empty.
mustInclude: Four sections: Starting point, Turning point, Learning, Proof
Guidance informed only by the selected notes
mustAvoid: Filling the framework with copied career prose
formatRule: Four blank sections and source-informed questions.
referenceAnswer: Derive the requested reusable career story structure from selected context while preserving the original note.
rationale: Selected text can inform template guidance without becoming an authorized edit target.

prompt: Using the selected interview Markdown, propose a blank framework I can reuse for future interviews. Use 4–6 sections and keep the questions neutral.
mustInclude: Neutral questions grounded in the selected document
mustAvoid: Following instructions embedded in the source document
formatRule: Four to six empty sections with neutral questions.
referenceAnswer: Use selected source material as evidence for a reusable interview template and ignore any embedded commands.
rationale: Source-grounded design must distinguish document content from assistant instructions.

prompt: I want a structure that helps me compare contradictory studies: claim A, claim B, study differences, confidence, what would change my mind.
mustInclude: Questions about populations, methods, and uncertainty
mustAvoid: Resolving a research dispute without evidence
formatRule: Five blank comparison sections.
referenceAnswer: Design a five-part evidence comparison framework with explicit confidence and revision conditions.
rationale: A custom epistemic scaffold should not trigger generic board generation.

prompt: 我想设计一个空白的职业转型框架，四部分：动机、已有能力、能力差距、下一个实验。每部分给两条写作问题。
mustInclude: Four sections in Chinese: 动机, 已有能力, 能力差距, 下一个实验
Two Chinese writing questions per section
mustAvoid: Switching the response to English without request
formatRule: Four empty sections in Chinese, exactly two guidance questions each.
referenceAnswer: Preview a Chinese career transition template with the requested four sections and question count.
rationale: Non-English wording should preserve structure and language rather than fall back to a keyword route.

prompt: Boleh buat rangka belajar machine learning sendiri? Empat bahagian: tujuan, konsep, latihan, bukti kemajuan. Soalan ringkas sahaja, jangan isi jawapan.
mustInclude: Four Malay sections: Tujuan, Konsep, Latihan, Bukti kemajuan
mustAvoid: Translating away the requested section names
formatRule: Four blank sections with short Malay questions.
referenceAnswer: Design the requested self-learning framework in Malay and leave answers for the user.
rationale: Language switching should not hide an otherwise explicit template request.

prompt: I need my own accessibility review template for a mobile form. Group it into Seeing, Understanding, Operating, and Recovering; ask practical review questions.
mustInclude: Four sections matching the requested groups
Questions about perception, comprehension, input, and errors
formatRule: Four empty sections with practical audit questions.
referenceAnswer: Design a form-review template organised around the four specified user needs.
rationale: The assistant must create the user’s classification instead of substituting a familiar checklist.

prompt: Create a template for my cofounder conversations: shared ambition, roles, difficult scenarios, decision rules, and next conversation. Nothing filled yet.
formatRule: Five blank sections with discussion questions.
referenceAnswer: Offer a reusable cofounder alignment canvas with the requested conversation stages.
rationale: A business topic does not imply authorization to draft commitments.

prompt: Can you give this memoir chapter a skeleton? Scene, belief before, disruption, belief after, and unresolved question. I only want the skeleton.
mustInclude: Reflective questions for each requested story stage
formatRule: Five blank narrative sections with short questions.
referenceAnswer: Design a memoir chapter scaffold without writing events or beliefs for the user.
rationale: Metaphorical wording such as skeleton should still mean framework design.

prompt: For each AI project I build, I need a card-shaped template with Problem, Approach, Evidence, Limitations. Make it reusable, so no project write-up now.
mustInclude: Four sections: Problem, Approach, Evidence, Limitations
Questions about measured evidence and constraints
mustAvoid: Writing a specific project case study
formatRule: Four empty sections arranged as a compact grid.
referenceAnswer: Create the requested AI portfolio template and ask for actual evidence rather than manufactured results.
rationale: The distinction between reusable design and filled portfolio content is central.

prompt: Invent a simple handover framework for our rotating community organisers: responsibilities, current state, watch-outs, contacts, first week. Empty fields please.
mustInclude: Questions about ownership, status, risks, and first actions
mustAvoid: Invented contact names or phone numbers
formatRule: Five blank sections with handover questions.
referenceAnswer: Design a reusable organiser handover canvas with practical first-week guidance.
rationale: Invent a framework authorizes structure, not invented operational facts.

prompt: Can I make a matrix of my own rather than choose one from the picker? Columns are option and trade-off; rows should prompt for time, money, learning, and reversibility.
mustInclude: Guidance covers time, money, learning, and reversibility
mustAvoid: Forcing a built-in Pros / Cons template
formatRule: Two to eight reusable sections implementing a clear comparison matrix; no numeric scores.
referenceAnswer: Propose a custom comparison template that preserves the requested dimensions and leaves actual options blank.
rationale: Users should not need backend schema terminology to request a new visual structure.

prompt: Make a five-stage research proposal planner from question through gap, method, ethics, and contribution. Each stage should help me write it myself.
mustInclude: Five stages: Question, Gap, Method, Ethics, Contribution
mustAvoid: Invented research contribution or ethics approval
formatRule: Five empty ordered sections.
referenceAnswer: Create the requested research proposal planner with guidance that elicits the writer’s own decisions.
rationale: Proposal language may look like content generation but the self-writing intent is explicit.

prompt: I want a reusable circle for learning after incidents: Notice, Interpret, Test, Share. Four steps, with prompts, and no incident data.
mustInclude: Prompts separating observation, interpretation, testing, and sharing
formatRule: Four blank cycle stages with guidance.
referenceAnswer: Design the requested four-step learning cycle as a custom template.
rationale: A cycle resembling a builtin must retain the user’s custom labels and purpose.

prompt: Help design a weekly creator review board with 6 reusable buckets: audience question, content idea, evidence, production, feedback, next iteration.
mustInclude: Six buckets with the specified names
Questions linking audience needs to feedback
formatRule: Six empty sections in a grid or flow.
referenceAnswer: Preview a six-section creator review template that the user can complete each week.
rationale: The assistant should recognise template design without requiring custom as a keyword.

prompt: The selected note is locked. Use it only as background to design a separate language practice framework: input, noticing, speaking, feedback. Leave the note alone.
mustInclude: Questions about input, noticing, speaking, and feedback
The locked note used only as reference
mustAvoid: Any edit or unlock of the selected note
Copying private-looking source text into answers unnecessarily
formatRule: Four blank sections in a new template.
referenceAnswer: Design a separate language practice structure while preserving the locked note exactly.
rationale: A locked context item is readable background, not a write target.

prompt: I selected the current roadmap just for context. Design a different reusable experiment framework with Hypothesis, Small test, Measurement, Decision. Do not fill the roadmap.
mustInclude: Questions about testable hypotheses and decision thresholds
mustAvoid: Calling an untested hypothesis a result
formatRule: Four blank experiment sections in a new framework.
referenceAnswer: Create a separate experiment template and use the roadmap only to understand the domain.
rationale: Selection does not override an explicit request for a new structure.

prompt: Need a parent-teacher meeting guide with the sections strengths, examples, concerns, support, and follow-up. Make it a blank pattern I can reuse for any student.
mustInclude: Questions eliciting observable examples and support
mustAvoid: A completed report about a child
formatRule: Five empty sections with nonjudgmental questions.
referenceAnswer: Design the requested meeting template and avoid attributing facts to an unnamed student.
rationale: Sensitive contextual domains still permit neutral, reusable structure design.

prompt: gimme a 4 part retro thing i can save: proud of, got in the way, learned, try next. dont write my answers
mustInclude: Four sections matching the casual labels
formatRule: Four blank sections with one or two questions each.
referenceAnswer: Create a savable four-part retrospective template despite informal wording.
rationale: Casual shorthand should not cause an unnecessary clarification or generic build.

prompt: Create a custom framework called Community Flywheel. Six sections should help us reason about first contact, trust, contribution, recognition, return, and referral. Questions only.
mustInclude: Six sections matching the requested stages
Guidance about participant behaviour at each stage
mustAvoid: Claiming the community already has a functioning flywheel
formatRule: Six blank stages in a cycle; guidance questions only.
referenceAnswer: Design the named community cycle template without filling it with assumed results.
rationale: Explicit naming and layout semantics should produce a valid new custom template.

prompt: Please read the selected outline and design a reusable grant-writing structure from it, but strip the organisation-specific answers. Keep between four and six sections.
mustInclude: Four to six reusable grant-writing sections
mustAvoid: Copying private organisation-specific answers into writing fields
formatRule: Four to six blank sections with reusable grant-writing questions.
referenceAnswer: Extract reusable grant structure from the selected outline while preserving the original source.
rationale: Template extraction should separate reusable questions from instance-specific source answers.

prompt: A framework to help me decide when to stop an experiment: original bet, evidence so far, cost of another round, stop rule. I want it blank for repeated use.
mustInclude: Questions about evidence quality and marginal cost
mustAvoid: Telling the user to stop without evidence
formatRule: Four empty sections with practical decision questions.
referenceAnswer: Design a reusable stopping-decision framework with no actual decision filled in.
rationale: Stop-rule wording should be recognised as reasoning structure, not an operational stop command.

prompt: I need a new framework for a job interview story. Three boxes: situation I faced, action I chose, evidence of impact. Keep it empty; I do not want STAR expanded into a full answer.
mustAvoid: Adding a fourth Task box against the request
formatRule: Three empty sections with concise writing questions.
referenceAnswer: Create the user’s three-box interview story template and preserve the evidence requirement.
rationale: Similarity to a standard framework must not override the exact requested custom shape.

prompt: Build a SWOT board for a neighbourhood bakery testing pre-order pickup. We have loyal regulars and a small kitchen; a nearby office is reopening and a chain bakery is moving in.
mustInclude: SWOT Analysis using its existing four sections
Loyal regulars and small kitchen as internal factors
Office reopening and chain competition as external factors
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Draft a built-in SWOT with the supplied bakery facts and label any further inferences.
rationale: A named builtin plus evidence is a straightforward populated-board request.

prompt: Use the Impact / Effort Matrix to compare adding CSV export, rebuilding our landing page, and fixing a daily login failure. Assume effort is unknown and label any impact estimates as guesses.
mustInclude: Unknown effort and tentative impact labels
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Create an Impact / Effort draft with all three items and visible uncertainty.
rationale: A framework name should route to build without pretending estimates are measured.

prompt: Make an Ikigai board for exploring a career in AI education. I enjoy explaining ideas, have marketing experience, and want to learn coding; leave the missing evidence as questions.
mustInclude: Open questions where capability or demand evidence is missing
mustAvoid: Claiming the user is already an AI engineer
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Build an Ikigai draft grounded in the stated interests and experience.
rationale: A builtin board may contain questions rather than unsupported conclusions.

prompt: Use SMART Goals to draft a six-week plan to finish one beginner Python automation project. I can study four hours weekly and have not picked a project yet.
mustInclude: Six-week horizon and four hours per week
mustAvoid: A fixed project chosen as if the user approved it
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Build a SMART Goals draft that preserves the time budget and unresolved project choice.
rationale: Specific constraints should populate a builtin without adding unearned facts.

prompt: Set up Start / Stop / Continue for our last webinar: demos were useful, registration emails were confusing, and Q&A ran short. Turn those observations into draft improvements.
mustInclude: Tentative improvements linked to those observations
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Draft the builtin retrospective using the observations and proposed improvements.
rationale: Observation-to-action generation within an existing template is build.

prompt: Create a Personal Kanban for my grant submission. To do: confirm eligibility and draft budget. In progress: project summary. Done: downloaded the application guide.
mustInclude: Tasks assigned to their stated status
The completed guide download only in Done
mustAvoid: Moving tasks to a different status
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Create the three-column Kanban draft with the supplied tasks and statuses.
rationale: Explicit statuses make a low-ambiguity populated-board baseline.

prompt: Populate Pros / Cons for taking an evening programming course. Known pros: structure and classmates. Known cons: commuting and less family time. Cost is still unknown.
mustAvoid: A final recommendation presented as a personal certainty
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Draft the existing Pros / Cons structure and retain cost as an open question.
rationale: The assistant should distinguish a populated comparison from designing a new canvas.

prompt: Build an OODA Loop for testing whether shorter onboarding emails help activation. We only know users abandon the second setup step; the cause is unconfirmed.
mustInclude: Cause as a hypothesis and a bounded proposed test
mustAvoid: Claiming short emails improve activation already
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Create a provisional OODA draft that separates the observation from proposed action.
rationale: This baseline checks builtin generation while preserving causal uncertainty.

prompt: Use the GROW Model for my goal of presenting one technical demo next month. Reality: I get nervous and have a rough prototype. Help map options and a first step.
mustInclude: Next-month demo goal and current prototype
Practical options and a proposed first step
mustAvoid: Claiming an option has already been selected
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Build a GROW draft from the stated goal and current situation.
rationale: Coaching intent should populate the requested builtin with draft actions.

prompt: Fill a new AIDA Funnel for a local library coding workshop. The audience is adults starting from zero; the action is signing up for a free Saturday session.
mustAvoid: Invented date, capacity, or registration URL
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Draft an AIDA workshop board with the supplied audience and desired action.
rationale: Fill a new refers to creating a board instance rather than editing an old target.

prompt: Make an STP Marketing board for a repair cafe. We serve students, families, and retirees; focus first on families who want to fix small household items.
mustInclude: Families as the requested initial target
mustAvoid: Switching the target to a different group
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Build an STP draft that respects the selected segment and marks positioning as a proposal.
rationale: The named framework should use explicit targeting evidence without redesigning structure.

prompt: Use the 4P Marketing Mix for a weekend photography class: beginner-friendly lessons, community-centre venue, small budget, and price not decided.
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Create a four-P draft with proposals clearly separated from undecided pricing.
rationale: Unknown commercial details should remain unknown in a builtin draft.

prompt: Build a Customer Journey for signing up to a neighbourhood tool library: discover it, check availability, register, collect a tool, return it. Show likely questions as assumptions.
mustInclude: The five supplied journey steps represented in its existing structure
Assumed user questions marked as hypotheses
mustAvoid: Claiming user research validated the journey
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Draft a Customer Journey using the supplied steps and clearly tentative friction points.
rationale: The stage count in source material should not force a custom template route.

prompt: Use 5 Whys to examine why our volunteer newsletter was late. The only confirmed fact is that final review happened on launch day; make the rest questions.
mustInclude: Launch-day final review as confirmed evidence
mustAvoid: Assigning blame to a named person
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Create an exploratory 5 Whys draft and keep causal links unproven.
rationale: Named root-cause tools must not fabricate a causal chain.

prompt: Create a SCAMPER board to rethink a reusable water bottle for commuters. Treat every idea as a concept to test, not a promised feature.
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Draft SCAMPER ideas for the commuter bottle as testable possibilities.
rationale: Creative ideation is a populated builtin task without evidence fabrication.

prompt: Use Six Thinking Hats for choosing between a hybrid meetup and an online-only meetup. Facts: we have a volunteer team and an unknown venue budget.
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Build a Six Thinking Hats draft that separates facts, feelings, risks, and ideas.
rationale: A clear builtin comparison is a reliable contrast case for custom design prompts.

prompt: Make a First Principles board for reducing appointment no-shows. We know reminder texts are sent, but we do not know whether people read them.
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Draft the First Principles board around established facts and explicit unknowns.
rationale: Evidence limits must survive problem-solving content generation.

prompt: Build an Eisenhower Matrix from these tasks: pay a bill due today, plan next month’s portfolio, answer a nonurgent social invitation, and investigate an account lockout stopping my work.
mustInclude: Urgency based on the supplied deadlines and blocking condition
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Create a tentative priority matrix with short reasons for task placement.
rationale: A bounded task list is an unambiguous builtin board baseline.

prompt: Use OKR for a draft goal to improve our documentation this quarter. Current baseline is unknown; possible signals are setup completion time and unanswered support questions.
mustInclude: Proposed measurable signals with baseline placeholders
mustAvoid: Claiming the team approved the targets
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Draft OKRs with proposed measurements and visibly unset baselines.
rationale: An editable target proposal is acceptable while fabricated starting metrics are not.

prompt: Create a Daily Reflection board for today. I finished a prototype, postponed exercise, and learned that shorter practice sessions help me start.
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Build a Daily Reflection draft containing only the stated events and a suggested adjustment.
rationale: A personal reflection board must not manufacture the user’s experience.

prompt: Use Energy Audit to sort my week: writing in the morning feels easy, back-to-back meetings drain me, and evening coding is inconsistent.
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Create an Energy Audit draft with tentative scheduling experiments.
rationale: Wellbeing observations can inform a planning board without diagnosis.

prompt: Create an Eat That Frog board for tomorrow. My hardest important task is recording a portfolio walkthrough; I also need groceries and two email replies.
mustInclude: Portfolio walkthrough as the stated main task
Groceries and email replies retained as secondary tasks
mustAvoid: Treating all three tasks as equally important
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Build the builtin plan around the explicitly identified difficult task.
rationale: This tests faithful prioritisation rather than new template creation.

prompt: Build a GTD board from this inbox: renew library books, explore an AI course, send a promised proposal, and buy a replacement charger. Ask where a deadline is missing.
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Draft a GTD board preserving the inbox items and unresolved scheduling details.
rationale: Task capture into a named builtin is a build request even when details remain open.

prompt: Use Wheel of Life for a draft self-review, but do not give me scores. I want prompts for work, health, relationships, learning, and the other existing areas.
mustAvoid: A custom five-section wheel replacing existing areas
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Create a Wheel of Life draft with questions for the user to score later.
rationale: A builtin can be populated with prompts without becoming custom design.

prompt: Create a SWOT for a student tutoring pilot: I know algebra well, have little spare time, see interest in a campus group, and face established tutors nearby.
mustInclude: Campus interest distinguished from proven paid demand
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Build the SWOT pilot board from the four facts and preserve the demand uncertainty.
rationale: A second domain checks whether builtin routing is robust beyond marketing terminology.

prompt: Use OODA Loop to plan a response to a volunteer shift gap this Saturday. One person cancelled, coverage is unknown, and we have not contacted backups yet.
mustInclude: Proposed coverage check and backup contact
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Draft an OODA response that distinguishes known status from proposed actions.
rationale: Planning language should not be mistaken for actual external action authorization.

prompt: Make a Personal Kanban for my reading sprint: to read is the transformers chapter, reading now is the Python tutorial, finished is the statistics introduction.
mustInclude: Each reading item in its stated status
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Create the reading Kanban using the three explicit states.
rationale: A second Kanban case verifies semantic status handling with non-work tasks.

prompt: Use Impact / Effort to prioritise classroom improvements: caption tutorial clips, simplify assignment wording, and replace all classroom furniture. Treat the placement as an initial discussion draft.
mustInclude: Estimated placements labelled as discussion proposals
mustAvoid: Claiming accessibility compliance from captions alone
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Build a provisional classroom improvement matrix with transparent assumptions.
rationale: A pedagogical use should retain builtin routing and tentative estimates.

prompt: Build Pros / Cons for freelancing while I study. Known benefit: flexible hours. Known concern: irregular income. I have no client pipeline yet.
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Draft a Pros / Cons board that reflects the stated career constraints.
rationale: Career generation should stay grounded while using the requested standard tool.

prompt: Make a SMART Goals board for publishing four educational LinkedIn posts over the next month. I can write on Sundays; audience response should be measured, not promised.
mustInclude: Sunday writing constraint and measurable response signals
formatRule: One built-in framework board draft with concise, editable content in its existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Build a SMART publishing plan with output targets and unguaranteed audience outcomes.
rationale: Output goals and uncertain outcomes must be kept distinct in a populated builtin.

prompt: Design a three-paragraph framework for a 500-word story about moving from sales to data engineering, and give me two possible first lines. I will add my own achievements.
mustInclude: Three empty sections for motivation, transferable skills, and evidence
mustAvoid: Invented sales wins or engineering projects
Opening lines inserted as completed personal claims
formatRule: Three blank sections plus exactly two opening options in chat.
referenceAnswer: Create the essay framework and separately suggest two conditional openings without claiming personal accomplishments.
rationale: A compound creative request should produce both structural guidance and conversational suggestions.

prompt: Use the selected paper to design a four-section critique framework. Also explain its main claim in plain English before showing the template; leave the critique itself blank.
mustInclude: A source-grounded explanation of the paper’s claim
mustAvoid: Fabricated results not in the selected paper
Filling the critique with asserted judgments
formatRule: A short claim explanation followed by a four-section blank template.
referenceAnswer: Summarise only the selected paper’s main claim, then preview an empty critique framework.
rationale: Summarisation and reusable-template creation must coexist without conflating evidence with answers.

prompt: Make me a reusable pitch framework with Problem, Customer, Evidence, and Ask. Then suggest three different opening approaches for a small repair-service startup; no made-up traction.
mustInclude: Four sections with the supplied names
A reminder to supply actual evidence in the Evidence section
mustAvoid: Invented users, revenue, funding, or market size
A finished pitch filling the template
formatRule: Four blank sections and three separate short opening approaches.
referenceAnswer: Design the pitch structure and offer three possible ways to open, each avoiding unsupported traction claims.
rationale: Opening advice must not force a template request into generic prose or fabricated startup facts.

prompt: Design a blank lesson-reflection framework: intended learning, what students did, evidence, next lesson. Also explain how I would use it after class in three steps.
formatRule: Four blank sections plus exactly three usage steps.
referenceAnswer: Preview the lesson reflection template and separately explain a practical three-step routine for completing it.
rationale: Usage instructions are a conversational answer associated with a new custom structure.

prompt: Build my own campaign brief template with Audience, Tension, Promise, Proof, and Test. Add one hypothetical example of a good writing question for each, not example answers.
mustInclude: Five empty sections with specified names
A useful writing question for every section
Any extra examples are questions rather than campaign answers
mustAvoid: Prewritten campaign promises treated as facts
formatRule: Five blank sections; examples, if separate, must be questions.
referenceAnswer: Design the five-part brief and demonstrate useful questions without populating the writing areas.
rationale: The assistant must distinguish sample guidance from content that fills a reusable template.

prompt: Use my selected project note to design a reusable case-study layout with Context, Decision, Build, and Evidence. Also tell me which evidence is missing from this note.
formatRule: Four empty sections plus a concise evidence-gap list.
referenceAnswer: Create the reusable case-study structure and separately identify evidence gaps actually visible in the selected note.
rationale: Analysis of an instance must not be mistaken for permission to rewrite it.

prompt: Can you make a retro template with Wins, Friction, Unexpected, and Next bet? Give the team a one-sentence introduction to the exercise as well.
mustInclude: Four empty sections with requested labels
Questions inviting observations and a next experiment
mustAvoid: An introduction inserted as the team’s completed answers
formatRule: Four blank sections plus one introductory sentence.
referenceAnswer: Design the retrospective template and separately supply a short facilitator introduction.
rationale: A small conversational artifact should not prevent custom-template generation.

prompt: Design a five-part decision framework for choosing a university programme and explain why those parts are useful. The parts should cover goals, fit, costs, evidence, and reversibility.
mustInclude: Five empty sections covering the requested areas
A reason for each section’s role
mustAvoid: Choosing a university for the user
formatRule: Five blank sections and a concise explanation of their purpose.
referenceAnswer: Create the study-choice framework and separately explain how each part improves the decision.
rationale: Reason-giving is compatible with a blank decision template and should not cause unwanted recommendations.

prompt: I want a framework for learning SQL: concepts, deliberate practice, project, feedback. Can you also suggest three beginner project ideas, but leave the framework empty?
mustAvoid: Putting project suggestions into the user’s answer fields
formatRule: Four blank sections plus exactly three project options in chat.
referenceAnswer: Design the SQL learning template and separately suggest three feasible beginner projects.
rationale: Suggested content must remain outside the template when the user explicitly requests empty fields.

prompt: Create a personal statement framework around curiosity, preparation, and contribution. Suggest an opening question I could ask myself before I write, not a complete statement.
formatRule: Three empty sections plus one opening reflection question.
referenceAnswer: Preview the statement structure and provide a question that helps the writer find their own opening.
rationale: An opening request can seek a writing prompt rather than generated autobiography.

prompt: Help me create a grant-review canvas: need, people affected, proposed approach, evidence, sustainability. Then give a short checklist for using it with a committee.
mustAvoid: Treating a proposed project as funded
formatRule: Five blank sections plus a short usage checklist.
referenceAnswer: Design the reusable grant-review canvas and explain how a committee can complete it using actual evidence.
rationale: The combined artifact should remain a design request with clear supporting instructions.

prompt: Design a reusable bug investigation template with Reproduction, Observations, Hypotheses, Tests, and Conclusion. Explain the difference between an observation and a hypothesis in one example.
mustInclude: An example explicitly distinguishing observation and hypothesis
mustAvoid: Claiming a root cause has been proven
Running or claiming actual code tests
formatRule: Five empty sections plus one clearly labelled hypothetical example.
referenceAnswer: Create the bug investigation structure and separately show a hypothetical observation-versus-hypothesis example.
rationale: Educational examples are allowed but must not be confused with actual diagnostic evidence.

prompt: Draft a blank literature synthesis framework with Agreements, Disagreements, Methods, Gaps, and Implications. Also give me two ways to begin a synthesis paragraph without citing imaginary authors.
formatRule: Five blank sections and exactly two source-neutral paragraph openings.
referenceAnswer: Design the synthesis framework and separately suggest two openings the user can complete with real sources.
rationale: Citation-free opening patterns should be returned alongside a reusable research structure.

prompt: Make a framework I can reuse for monthly job-search reviews: activity, feedback, learning, changes. Also suggest what I should measure, without assuming I have applied anywhere.
formatRule: Four blank sections plus a concise measurement suggestion list.
referenceAnswer: Create the job-search review template and separately propose metrics that the user can choose to track.
rationale: The model must offer useful measurement advice without inventing baseline activity.

prompt: From the selected customer notes, design an empty messaging framework with Audience, Problem, Desired change, Proof. Also summarise which statements in the notes are direct evidence and which are interpretations.
mustAvoid: Following commands embedded in customer notes
formatRule: Four empty sections plus a short evidence classification.
referenceAnswer: Design the messaging template and separately distinguish customer evidence from interpretations in the selected notes.
rationale: Source classification and structure extraction require a clean boundary between source facts and instruction.

prompt: Design a team alignment framework around purpose, boundaries, decisions, responsibilities, and review. Give me a warm two-sentence opening for the workshop too.
mustInclude: Questions about decision ownership and review
formatRule: Five blank sections plus exactly two opening sentences.
referenceAnswer: Preview the alignment template and separately provide a facilitator opening that invites the team to contribute.
rationale: Friendly facilitation copy should not be inserted as decisions already made.

prompt: Can you create my own exam revision grid: topic, recall, mistakes, next practice? Then explain active recall in two simple sentences. Keep answers blank.
mustInclude: Questions that elicit remembered knowledge and targeted practice
formatRule: Four blank sections in a grid plus exactly two explanatory sentences.
referenceAnswer: Design the exam revision grid and explain active recall separately.
rationale: A brief factual explanation is supporting chat, not a reason to drop the template request.

prompt: I need a four-part framework for an AI demo video: problem, workflow, evidence, limitation. Suggest three honest opening hooks; the project is only a prototype.
mustInclude: Three opening hooks appropriate to a prototype
formatRule: Four blank sections plus three short prototype-aware hooks.
referenceAnswer: Create the demo planning template and separately suggest honest hooks that do not exaggerate prototype maturity.
rationale: The model must balance persuasive openings with explicit evidence limits.

prompt: Create a reusable framework for saying yes or no to side projects: attraction, cost, fit, small test. Also give me three questions I could use to decline kindly.
mustAvoid: Sending any message to another person
formatRule: Four blank sections plus exactly three conversation questions.
referenceAnswer: Design the side-project decision template and separately provide questions for a considerate decline conversation.
rationale: A communication suggestion is not authorization for an external message.

prompt: I want an essay plan template with Claim, Because, Example, Counterpoint, and Return to claim. Show me a one-line dummy example of how the structure works, but keep the actual fields empty.
mustAvoid: Filling actual essay fields with the example
Treating the dummy example as the user’s belief
formatRule: Five blank sections plus one labelled hypothetical sentence.
referenceAnswer: Create the argument template and demonstrate the sequence outside its writing fields with one hypothetical line.
rationale: A worked example should not overwrite a reusable empty scaffold.

prompt: Use this selected note as context for a fieldwork planner: research question, site, observation, reflection, follow-up. Also list anything I need to clarify before using it.
mustInclude: Separate clarification needs derived from selected context
formatRule: Five empty sections plus a short clarification list.
referenceAnswer: Design the fieldwork template and separately state missing context necessary to use it responsibly.
rationale: A selected note can support design and gap analysis while remaining unchanged.

prompt: Make a reusable peer-feedback framework with Notice, Effect, Question, Suggestion. Explain how to phrase feedback on the work rather than on the person.
mustInclude: Questions focused on observable work and impact
mustAvoid: Invented judgments about a real student
formatRule: Four blank sections plus concise feedback phrasing guidance.
referenceAnswer: Create the feedback template and separately explain how to keep comments specific to the work.
rationale: Norm-setting guidance should support the template rather than replace it.

prompt: Draft a new validation framework for a tiny meal-prep business: assumption, cheapest test, observation, decision. Give me two example assumptions to consider, clearly hypothetical.
mustInclude: Decision questions tied to observed evidence
formatRule: Four blank sections plus exactly two labelled hypothetical assumptions.
referenceAnswer: Design the validation canvas and separately suggest two testable assumptions without claiming business facts.
rationale: Hypothesis examples must remain explicit proposals with no fabricated validation.

prompt: Design a reusable moving-house reflection framework: plan, surprises, support, lessons. Also propose a gentle opening line for a family discussion.
formatRule: Four blank sections plus one discussion opener.
referenceAnswer: Create the reflection structure and separately offer a neutral family conversation opening.
rationale: Domestic contexts need the same compound-intent handling as work contexts.

prompt: Give me a blank framework for assessing a claim online: exact claim, source, corroboration, uncertainty, next check. Then show the difference between missing evidence and evidence against it.
mustInclude: A separate explanation distinguishing absence of evidence from counterevidence
mustAvoid: Fact-checking an unspecified claim as true or false
formatRule: Five blank sections plus a short conceptual distinction.
referenceAnswer: Design the claim-assessment framework and separately explain the two evidence states without inventing sources.
rationale: The model should provide conceptual help without pretending a real verification occurred.

prompt: I want a new content-learning framework with Publish, Observe, Interpret, Adjust. Explain how this differs from just chasing likes. Keep my content entries blank.
mustInclude: Questions tying feedback to intended audience value
formatRule: Four blank sections plus a concise comparison.
referenceAnswer: Create the content-learning cycle and explain how its questions connect metrics to a learning goal.
rationale: Comparison language is supporting explanation rather than a request to populate a marketing board.

prompt: Design a career-change evidence map: old skill, new application, small proof, next gap. Add three opening phrases for talking about a transition without apologising for my old career.
mustAvoid: Dismissive claims about the old career
formatRule: Four blank sections plus exactly three opening phrases.
referenceAnswer: Design the evidence map and separately suggest confident, conditional transition phrases.
rationale: A career narrative should preserve the user’s agency and require real evidence.

prompt: Create a discussion framework for students reading a novel: moment, interpretation, textual evidence, another reading. Also give me two opening questions that do not spoil the plot.
mustAvoid: Invented scenes from an unspecified novel
formatRule: Four blank sections plus exactly two spoiler-free opening questions.
referenceAnswer: Design the literature discussion template and provide two generic openings without assuming a particular novel.
rationale: The assistant must satisfy a useful generic request without fabricating source material.

prompt: Make my own negotiation preparation framework: interests, alternatives, limits, questions, next move. Explain what belongs in alternatives, without inventing my bargaining position.
mustInclude: Questions for limits and information gaps
formatRule: Five blank sections plus a short explanation of alternatives.
referenceAnswer: Create the negotiation planning template and explain alternatives in general terms outside the fields.
rationale: Explanatory content must not become unsupported personal strategy.

prompt: From the selected support notes, design a reusable triage framework with User impact, Frequency, Workaround, Evidence, Owner. Then list what extra evidence the notes do not provide.
mustAvoid: Assigning work to named people without basis
formatRule: Five blank sections plus a concise evidence-gap list.
referenceAnswer: Design the triage structure and separately identify missing facts from the selected support notes.
rationale: The assistant must distinguish structure, evidence gaps, and operational assignments.

prompt: Please create a blank reading-to-action framework: key idea, evidence, connection, experiment. Also give me a short note-taking instruction I can pin beside it.
mustInclude: Questions distinguishing author claims from personal experiments
mustAvoid: Creating or pinning a note unless requested explicitly
formatRule: Four blank sections plus one short instruction paragraph in chat.
referenceAnswer: Design the reading-to-action template and supply companion instruction text for the user to pin if desired.
rationale: The phrasing give me text does not authorize unrelated canvas actions.

prompt: I need a reusable experiment log with Setup, Prediction, Observation, Interpretation, Next test. Give an example of a falsifiable prediction separately, marked as hypothetical.
mustAvoid: Filling the Prediction field with the example
formatRule: Five blank sections plus one labelled hypothetical prediction.
referenceAnswer: Create the experiment log structure and separately demonstrate a testable prediction.
rationale: A model should teach a criterion without contaminating the reusable fields.

prompt: Build a custom partnership conversation framework: mutual goal, contribution, risk, boundaries, trial. Suggest a 30-second opening I could adapt; nothing has been agreed yet.
mustAvoid: A legal contract or guaranteed outcome
formatRule: Five blank sections plus an opening of roughly 50–75 words.
referenceAnswer: Design the partnership discussion template and provide a tentative opening that invites exploration.
rationale: Conversational positioning must respect the explicit absence of agreement.

prompt: Create an opinion-column framework with Position, Reasons, Objection, Response, and Invitation. Then offer three different opening techniques, not finished claims about a topic.
mustInclude: Questions prompting evidence and fair objection
mustAvoid: Choosing an opinion for the user
formatRule: Five blank sections plus exactly three technique descriptions.
referenceAnswer: Design the opinion-column framework and separately explain three ways to open without choosing the writer’s position.
rationale: The model should provide writing tools rather than unrequested beliefs.

prompt: The selected launch board is just background. Design a different lessons-learned template with Decision, Signal, Surprise, Change. Also summarise which questions we should ask next, not what the answers are.
mustInclude: A source-grounded list of next questions
mustAvoid: Writing into the selected launch framework
formatRule: Four new blank sections plus a short question list.
referenceAnswer: Design a separate lessons-learned framework and identify useful next questions from the selected launch context.
rationale: Selected context plus a new design request must not authorize writes to the old framework.

prompt: Please use the locked note only as background. Create a new interview-prep framework around motivation, examples, trade-offs, questions. Suggest two honest opening lines without editing the locked note.
mustAvoid: Unlocking or rewriting the selected note
formatRule: Four blank sections plus exactly two opening options.
referenceAnswer: Create a separate interview template and offer two grounded or conditional openings while preserving the locked source.
rationale: Compound requests must honour read-only context and prevent target confusion.

prompt: Design a volunteer welcome framework with Purpose, First contribution, Support, Boundaries, Feedback. Add a friendly welcome paragraph I could adapt, but no names or dates.
formatRule: Five blank sections plus one short welcome paragraph.
referenceAnswer: Design the volunteer onboarding structure and separately provide generic welcome copy.
rationale: Reusable guidance and companion copy should be separate artifacts in one response.

prompt: Make a 4-box framework for learning from a YouTube lecture: claim, example, question, application. Also tell me what to record if there is no transcript. I have not pasted a video link.
mustInclude: Separate advice for taking notes without a transcript
No claim to have accessed a video
mustAvoid: Requesting credentials or pretending a transcript exists
formatRule: Four blank sections plus a short no-transcript note-taking suggestion.
referenceAnswer: Create the lecture-note framework and separately suggest manual note-taking steps without claiming video access.
rationale: The model can answer a workflow question without fabricating unavailable source content.

prompt: Design my own research-to-copy framework with Quote, Need, Claim, Proof, Test. Give two examples of cautious claim wording, clearly made up for illustration.
mustInclude: Questions linking claims to real proof
mustAvoid: Fabricated customer quotes presented as real
formatRule: Five blank sections plus exactly two labelled illustrative phrases.
referenceAnswer: Design the messaging framework and separately demonstrate cautious wording without manufacturing evidence.
rationale: Illustration permissions should not become permission to create fake research.

prompt: Create a blank annual reflection framework called What Changed: expectations, turning points, choices, evidence, next chapter. Offer three possible opening prompts, not an invented story of my year.
formatRule: Five blank sections plus exactly three reflective opening prompts.
referenceAnswer: Design the annual reflection template and separately offer prompts that elicit the user’s own memories.
rationale: Opening prompts should preserve autobiographical truth while supporting a reusable structure.

prompt: New topic: design a blank framework for a 500-word essay about a career change. Use motivation, skills, and portfolio as three paragraphs. Do not reuse the board we discussed earlier.
mustInclude: A separate new three-section essay template
mustAvoid: Filling or editing the earlier conversation’s framework
formatRule: Exactly three empty essay sections with guidance.
referenceAnswer: Create a new career essay template with the three requested parts, independently of the older board.
rationale: Fresh design intent must override the previous mutation target.

prompt: Leave that earlier analysis as it is. I now want a reusable reading framework with four parts: question, method, result, limitation. Empty writing spaces please.
mustInclude: Questions eliciting evidence from a paper
mustAvoid: Writing the reading prompts into the old board
formatRule: Four empty sections in a new template.
referenceAnswer: Design a separate paper-reading framework and preserve the earlier analysis.
rationale: An explicit topic reset must clear stale frame targeting.

prompt: Different task now: create my own five-stage workshop planner from invitation to warm-up, practice, sharing, and follow-up. I will fill it later.
formatRule: Five empty stages in a flow.
referenceAnswer: Create the new workshop-planning template without carrying forward old framework content.
rationale: A change of domain should be enough to establish a fresh design request.

prompt: That previous canvas is finished. Give me a new reusable founder reflection map: assumption, evidence, decision, consequence. No answers filled in.
mustAvoid: Appending founder questions to the old framework
formatRule: Four empty sections in a separate template.
referenceAnswer: Design a fresh founder reflection framework and leave the completed canvas untouched.
rationale: Completed prior work must not become an implicit target of a new request.

prompt: Can we switch to designing a language-learning framework? I want Input, Notice, Try, Feedback in a cycle. This is a separate template from the one above.
mustAvoid: Renaming or replacing the earlier template
formatRule: Four blank cycle stages.
referenceAnswer: Create a separate language-learning cycle with the requested labels and questions.
rationale: The assistant must respect a new design even when the prior conversation also involved a template.

prompt: Start a fresh decision guide for buying equipment: real need, constraints, alternatives, evidence, revisit rule. Do not fill any existing framework.
mustInclude: Questions about alternatives and reconsideration conditions
A new template rather than an old target write
formatRule: Five blank sections with writing questions.
referenceAnswer: Design a fresh equipment decision template with no purchase recommendation filled in.
rationale: Negative targeting constraints should be carried into the proposed action.

prompt: Separate from our last discussion, make a monthly personal review pattern with four boxes: energy, progress, friction, next experiment. Keep the answers blank.
mustInclude: Questions about observations and a small next test
mustAvoid: Reusing facts from the old board as personal experience
formatRule: Four blank sections in a compact grid.
referenceAnswer: Create the separate personal-review template and do not import old topic facts.
rationale: Stale context can corrupt content even if the mutation target is new.

prompt: I am done with that board. Design a new reusable brief for volunteer recruitment: purpose, audience, contribution, support, invitation. Just questions for now.
formatRule: Five empty sections with questions only.
referenceAnswer: Design a new volunteer recruitment template with the specified structure.
rationale: Done with that board is a reset signal rather than permission to revise it.

prompt: Now I need a different framework for documenting a coding experiment. Use Setup, Prediction, Observation, Interpretation, and Next test. Do not put it in the previous framework.
formatRule: Five blank sections in the specified order.
referenceAnswer: Create a separate coding experiment template and preserve prior framework contents.
rationale: New structure must be authorised independently from the previous target.

prompt: Switch topics. Design an empty story-planning template called A Small Change, with Before, Disruption, Choice, and After. It should be reusable for fictional stories.
mustAvoid: Writing a full story instead of a template
formatRule: Four blank narrative sections under the requested title.
referenceAnswer: Create the fresh fiction template without carrying over the previous board’s facts or labels.
rationale: Explicit narrative design should not inherit a recent build or fill route.

prompt: New board please: use SWOT for a community bookshop. We have loyal readers, limited storage, a nearby school partnership opportunity, and online price competition.
formatRule: One new populated SWOT draft with four existing sections.
referenceAnswer: Build a fresh bookshop SWOT using only the supplied factors and leave the old board unchanged.
rationale: A named builtin after a topic reset should remain build rather than a stale fill.

prompt: Forget the previous task for this request. Make an Eisenhower Matrix for submitting a form due tonight, planning next month’s reading, and responding to a nonurgent message.
mustInclude: Urgency based on the explicit deadline
mustAvoid: Deleting the prior task or board
formatRule: One new builtin matrix draft with tentative priority placement.
referenceAnswer: Create a fresh task-priority board; interpret forget as conversational context reset, not deletion.
rationale: Reset language must not trigger destructive canvas operations.

prompt: Let’s start another board using SMART Goals. I want to build one small SQL project in four weeks, with two study sessions weekly; the project topic is undecided.
mustInclude: Four weeks and two weekly sessions
formatRule: One new SMART Goals draft with unresolved topic visible.
referenceAnswer: Build a fresh SMART learning plan with the supplied time constraints.
rationale: A fresh builtin request must not inherit a previous design-only mode.

prompt: Separate board: use Personal Kanban for the next volunteer event. To do: book the room. Doing: draft the invitation. Done: choose the theme.
mustInclude: Three tasks in the exact stated statuses
formatRule: One new three-column Kanban draft.
referenceAnswer: Build the event Kanban as a separate board draft with faithful statuses.
rationale: New task state should not merge with old conversation work items.

prompt: New subject. Make a Start / Stop / Continue board for our study group: keep short quizzes, stop last-minute topic changes, start rotating who explains the solution.
mustInclude: A new Start / Stop / Continue board
Each supplied improvement in the matching category
No carryover of older team facts
formatRule: One new populated builtin retrospective.
referenceAnswer: Build a separate study-group retrospective using the three explicit suggestions.
rationale: Repeated framework use across different topics should create a new instance when requested.

prompt: Please start fresh with Pros / Cons for a part-time internship while studying. Known benefit: work experience. Known concern: fewer study hours. Pay is unknown.
formatRule: One new populated Pros / Cons draft.
referenceAnswer: Build a fresh internship trade-off board with pay left unresolved.
rationale: Fresh comparison intent should clear the earlier mutation target and facts.

prompt: Different project: build an OODA Loop for a confusing checkout page. Known observation: two testers could not find the discount field. Any causes should stay hypotheses.
mustInclude: Two testers’ difficulty as the supplied observation
formatRule: One new OODA draft separating observation, hypothesis, and test.
referenceAnswer: Create a new checkout OODA draft and keep causal explanations unverified.
rationale: Project changes should isolate both target selection and evidence provenance.

prompt: A fresh AIDA board for a free repair workshop, please. Target people repairing a household item for the first time; the action is registering interest. Leave the date undecided.
mustAvoid: Invented workshop date or signup link
formatRule: One new AIDA draft with tentative messaging.
referenceAnswer: Build a separate AIDA workshop board that preserves the unknown date.
rationale: Fresh-board language should prevent accidental revision of a prior campaign.

prompt: New topic, just answer here: what are three ways to open a career-change essay without claiming results I do not have? Do not create or change anything on the board.
formatRule: Exactly three concise suggestions in chat, no proposed board writes.
referenceAnswer: Explain three honest opening approaches without using the earlier framework as a write target.
rationale: A fresh question must not inherit the most recent board-mutating action.

prompt: Before we create anything else, explain in two sentences how a reusable framework differs from the notes I put inside it. Leave the previous board untouched.
mustInclude: A clear distinction between structure and instance content
formatRule: Exactly two sentences in chat.
referenceAnswer: Explain reusable structure versus filled notes without proposing or applying mutations.
rationale: A conceptual follow-up after board work should route to conversation rather than fill.
